blocks.text: An API key is required to access the publicly available set of ZPA APIs. An API key consists of a client ID and a client secret. Both are required for authentication prior to accessing the publicly available set of ZPA APIs.

Generating an API key only occurs in the Zscaler Admin Console from the API Keys page. Client IDs are always accessible from the page. Client secrets are only displayed when the key is first created, and they are not available in the saved configuration.
API keys provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Authenticate and access the ZPA APIs.
Generate the client ID and client secret used to access the ZPA APIs.

blocks.text: On the API Keys page (Administration > API > Private Access API), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Click Copy ID. Within the menu, you can:
Copy your customer ID. The customer ID is needed for making AP calls.
Copy your Microtenant ID. The Microtenant ID is the unique identifier of the Microtenant, and is needed for making API calls if you're within a Microtenant.

The Copy Microtenant ID action is only visible if you are within a Microtenant. If you are within a Microtenant, then you must pass the microtenantId when making an API call. To learn more, see Getting Started and Configuring Microtenants Using API.
Add an API key.
Filter the information that appears in the table. By default, no filters are applied. To learn more, see Using Tables.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
View a list of API keys. For each key, you can see:
Name: The name of the API key.
Client ID: The ID for the key. It is needed to access the ZPA API Portal.
Status: Indicates whether the key is enabled or disabled.
Session Validity Interval (In Seconds): The amount of time in seconds that the key remains active before expiring.
Creation Date: The date and time the API key was created.

Role: The predefined role or a custom role of the API key (e.g., API Full Access, API Read Only). Roles for API keys enforce granular role-based access control (RBAC) on all publicly available ZPA API operations. To learn more, see Understanding Role-Based Access Control for ZPA API, Adding API Keys, About API Clients, and Adding an API Client.

If you are subscribed to Authentication Service and have it enabled for your tenant, API keys created in Authentication Service appear on the API Keys page in the Zscaler Admin Console and are read only. To learn more, see What Is Authentication Service?
Copy a client ID.
Edit an API key.
Delete an API key.
If an API key is configured using Zscaler Deception, then the edit and delete options are unavailable.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
